bitrate.aboutText: Bitrate is the amount of data you send to Twitch per second. It depends on resolution, FPS, and visual quality (BPP). Too low bitrate causes pixelation, too high causes buffering for viewers. Twitch recommends a maximum of 6000 kbps for affiliates and 8500 kbps for partners. Adjust these values based on your upload connection and content type.
bitrate.obsGuideDesc: Apply these values in OBS Studio for an optimal stream. Go to Settings → Output.

avatars.title: Chat Avatars
avatars.subtitle: Small interactive avatars that react to chat and events. Your viewers can make their avatars dance, jump, or interact with the environment.
avatars.enableDesc: Enables the interactive avatar system on the overlay. Your viewers' avatars will appear and react.
avatars.themeDesc: The style of the avatars that will be shown on stream.
avatars.themeDefaultDesc: Small friendly, fun, and colorful robots.
avatars.themeCyberpunkDesc: Avatars with dark neon aesthetics, visors, and cybernetic augmentations.
avatars.theme8bitsDesc: Classic NES/Game Boy style characters with square pixels.
avatars.themeHordeDesc: Fierce Horde orc warriors with red war armor and tribal war paint.
avatars.limitsDesc: Adjust the amount of avatars and physics to optimize your overlay's performance.
avatars.chatBubbles: Show chat messages as speech bubbles above avatars
avatars.commandsDesc: Allow viewers to control their avatars by typing commands in the Twitch chat.
avatars.eventsDesc: Select which events the avatars should react to automatically.
avatars.eventSub: New Subscription (they do a big joy jump)
avatars.overlayDesc: Copy this URL and add it as a Browser Source in OBS (full size recommended, e.g. 1920x1080).
avatars.betaInfoText: The avatar system is in an experimental phase. Currently, it shows basic shapes that react to events with full physics, preparing the ground for the full sprites. It does not affect or break any other StreamDaemon functionality. If you encounter issues, you can disable it from the main switch.

streamAvatar.title: Live Avatar
streamAvatar.subtitle: Display an animated avatar on screen that moves its mouth in sync with your microphone. Perfect to replace or complement your webcam.
streamAvatar.enableDesc: Enable the lip-sync avatar on the overlay.
streamAvatar.streamAvatarDefaultDesc: Friendly vector avatar with soft expressions.
streamAvatar.streamAvatarCyberDesc: Dark neon aesthetic for cyberpunk streams.
streamAvatar.streamAvatarPixelDesc: Retro look with flat colors and sharp edges.
streamAvatar.streamAvatarFutureDesc: Robotic appearance with cool metallic tones.
streamAvatar.streamAvatarDarkDesc: Shadowy palette with pale skin and dark clothes.
streamAvatar.obsDesc: Add this URL as a Browser Source in OBS to show the avatar on your scene.
streamAvatar.chromaKeyDesc: Useful for removing the background in OBS with a chroma key filter.
streamAvatar.customAvatarDesc: Upload a ZIP with the PNG images: body.png, eyes-open.png, eyes-closed.png, mouth-closed.png, mouth-slight.png, mouth-open.png, mouth-wide.png and mouth-round.png.
